previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with a history of dilated cardiomyopathy, atrial fibrillation, and type 2 diabetes was admitted for acute decompensated systolic heart failure, presenting with worsening dyspnea on exertion, orthopnea, and mild lower extremity edema. The exacerbation was attributed to noncompliance with his diuretic regimen and recent consumption of high-sodium foods. Initial evaluation revealed an elevated proBNP of 2820, mild pulmonary vascular congestion on chest imaging, and an INR of 5.9 due to an inadvertent warfarin dose increase. The patient was treated with IV furosemide and transitioned to oral torsemide 120 mg daily, achieving a weight reduction from 117.1 kg to 111.6 kg. His INR was managed by holding warfarin for one day and restarting at 2.5 mg daily. Elevated liver enzymes and bilirubin were attributed to congestive hepatopathy, requiring outpatient follow-up. The patient showed improvement in symptoms and was discharged home with optimized heart failure therapy, instructions to monitor weight, and plans for cardiology follow-up regarding ICD placement.

Brief Hospital Course:
Patient is a ___ year old male with history of Afib c/b stroke 
when subtherapeutic on Coumadin, heart failure (EF 30%), gout, 
and IDDM presenting with melena and anemia from GI bleed. 

#GI bleed: Patient presented with Hgb drop 4 pts below baseline 
(10 from 14) and melena in setting of 600 ibuprofen q4 x 2 weeks 
while on warfarin. Was hypotensive to 80/50 in the ED but 
declined blood transfusion and was treated with IVF, K centra, 
and vitamin K to reverse (therapeutic) INR. He underwent EGD, 
which showed diffuse ulceration of the gastric mucosa with no 
active site of bleeding. He was prescribed Protonix 40 mg BID, 
which he should take for 8 weeks to allow his stomach lining to 
heal. Hgb was stable during the admission and warfarin was 
restarted. 

#Lumbar stenosis
The patient has fairly severe pseudoclaudication of the R leg, 
which is the original pain complaint that caused him to present 
to the ED when he was prescribed ibuprofen. MRI showed 
impingement of a nerve root on the right, which correlates with 
the distribution of his symptoms. As he is not a candidate for 
NSAIDs, he was prescribed oxycodone for pain; he will follow up 
with his PCP for ongoing pain control. He was also referred to a 
spine surgeon, since he was interested in discussing 
laminectomy. He has heart failure and history of a stroke, but 
if optimized carefully he would appear to still be a reasonable 
surgical candidate.

#Chronic heart failure:  
Non-ischemic cardiomyopathy with LVEF 30%. He appears euvolemic 
at discharge after bleeding followed by cautious fluids. 
Torsemide is restarted at discharge. He is continued on his ACE, 
beta blocker and spironolactone.

#NSVT
Patient declines an ICD for his reduced LFEV. He was observed to 
have NSVT up to 15 beats during this admission. He was 
extensively educated on the risk of sudden cardiac death, but 
this is an outcome that does not seem too philosophically 
troubling to him. He will follow up with cardiology.

#Atrial Fibrillation:  
His warfarin was reversed for GI bleed but has been restarted at 
discharge. He was offered bridging anticoagulation due to 
history of stroke but declined this. 

# S/p pars plana vitrectomy of the left eye (___) for 
non-clearing vitreous hemorrhage.  
Patient reported new floaters; ophtho was consulted. Trace 
vitreous hemorrhage without obvious active bleeding site. 
Periphery is attached and shows no evidence of retinal tear or 
detachment. Outpatient f/u scheduled

Discharge Instructions:
GI BLEED
You had bleeding from your stomach lining because you were given 
Ibuprofen for pain when you were taking warfarin. You had an 
endoscopy and it looked like damage that would heal up if you 
took an antacid for a few weeks and didn't take any more 
ibuprofen. We had held your warfarin while it was actively 
bleeding, but you should be able to take this safely again now. 

LEG PAIN
We did am MRI that showed your pain is caused by lumbar 
stenosis, which is where nerves get pinched was they emerge from 
your lumbar (lower) spine. We are giving your Tylenol (take 
regularly) and oxycodone (take as needed). Because the 
underlying cause is degenerative arthritis of the bones of your 
spine, the only way to fix this problem is surgery.

HEART RHYTHM:
Due to your heart disease, you are at a very high risk for going 
into an unstable heart rhythm. This can cause sudden death! The 
treatment is a defibrillator that can automatically shock you 
and bring you back if this happens. You probably would need one 
of these before being a candidate for back surgery.

HEART FAILURE:
Weigh yourself every morning, call MD if weight goes up more 
than 3 lbs, or if your weight goes down and you start to feel 
lightheaded.

The pelvic girdle is congruent, without SI joint or pubic symphysis diastasis.
Assessment of sacrum is limited by overlying bowel gas, but, where visible,,
it is grossly unremarkable.  Prominent transverse processes at the

The bowel gas pattern is non-specific, with stool noted in the colon.

IMPRESSION:

pelvis.

EXAMINATION:  MR ___ SPINE W/O CONTRAST ___ MR SPINE

INDICATION:  ___ year old man with R knee/hip/thigh pain c/w
pseudoclaudication; pain localizes to roughly L3/L4 dermatomes. Assess for
?lumbar stenosis

TECHNIQUE:  Sagittal imaging was performed with T2, T1, and STIR technique,
followed by axial T2 imaging.

COMPARISON:  CT of the abdomen and pelvis from ___.

FINDINGS: 

Alignment is normal.  Vertebral body signal intensity appears normal.  There
is diffuse degenerative disc desiccation throughout the lumbar spine.  The
spinal cord appears to be unremarkable, with the conus medullaris terminating
at T12- L1.

T12-L1:  There is no significant spinal canal or neural foraminal narrowing at
this level.

L1-L2:  There is a minimal disc bulge with no significant encroachment on the
spinal canal or neural foramina.

L2-L3:  There is a bulge of the disc and a midline and right-sided protrusion.
The disc protrusion compresses the thecal sac and the traversing right L3
nerve root.  The neural foramina appear normal in spite of small facet
osteophytes.

L3-L4:  Bulging of the disc combines with ligamentum flavum thickening and
facet osteophytes to produce moderate spinal canal narrowing.  The disc bulge
compresses the traversing L4 nerve roots against the facet osteophytes
bilaterally.  There is a small disc fragment extending superiorly along the
posterior margin of the L3 vertebral body at the right lateral aspect of the
spinal canal.  This also contributes to right L4 nerve root compression.

L4-L5:  There is mild bulging of the disc with no significant spinal canal or
neural foraminal compromise.  There is small facet osteophytes bilaterally.

L5-S1: There is minimal bulging of the disc with no significant spinal canal
narrowing. Intervertebral osteophytes and facet osteophytes produce mild left
neural foraminal narrowing

No paraspinal or paravertebral soft tissue abnormalities are identified.

IMPRESSION:


1. Degenerative disc disease most marked at L2-3 where there is spinal canal
narrowing and compression of the right-sided nerve roots by a disc protrusion.
2. Small disc protrusion with a superiorly migrating fragment on the right at
L3-4.  This compresses the traversing L4 nerve root.  .
